clue.text: Carriers taking issue with egg on one sent into cleaners

definitions.note: issue means offspring, so these are carriers that take children along

parts.note: to egg someone on is to push or urge them

indicators.note: a piece sent into another is placed inside it

parts.note: chars, short for charwomen, are cleaners
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Cleaning staff object when someone eggs on a newcomer sent to join them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a quarrel but means children, so the carriers are ones that take babies along.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies, a parent's issue, ride in wheeled seats pushed along the pavement.

clue.text: Authorise advance

definitions.meaning: to authorise a law or motion is to approve it formally
an advance is an amorous approach

explanation.surface: A manager signs off on a payment in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament approves bills formally; an amorous approach to someone is also this word.

clue.text: Views covering African organisation's meetings

indicators.note: one word covering another wraps around it

parts.note: to view is to see, so views is sees
the ANC is the African National Congress; the 's is part of the possessive surface

explanation.surface: Opinions are recorded about an African body's meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: The African National Congress is South Africa's governing party.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualist sittings are gatherings held to contact the dead.

clue.text: Folds, once ratings go badly

indicators.note: letters treated badly are knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Sheep pens were once judged poorly by inspectors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like the verb of the surface but is part of the fodder, which 'badly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold is a church flock, the body of worshippers gathered under one pastor.

clue.text: Juggling act — lithe, fit and active

indicators.note: juggling tosses things about, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A supple juggling act shows the performer to be in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporty and in good physical condition is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Plans right employment laws at last

parts.note: employment of something is its use

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of laws

explanation.surface: Proposals on employment rights finally become law.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricks and stratagems are cunning schemes, so plans in a devious sense.

clue.text: Not so many will dismiss female in this vessel

indicators.note: to dismiss something is to send it away, so that letter goes

parts.note: not so many means fewer

explanation.surface: Fewer people will fire the woman aboard this ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large water jug is a container, which is one sense of vessel.

clue.text: Women anticipating skipper's lie

indicators.note: anticipating means coming before, so W leads

parts.note: a skipper is anything that skips, so a hopper

explanation.surface: Women expect the ship's captain to be dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' looks like a captain but is literally something that skips.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge fib or barefaced untruth is colloquially called by this word.

clue.text: Almost deserved to be set up in lease giving privacy

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: rent is what is paid under a lease

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so read backwards
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: deserved means merited

explanation.surface: A lease offering seclusion was almost deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims MERITED to MERITE; 'to be set up' turns it to ETIREM, placed 'in' RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Seclusion, withdrawal from society, is a state of solitude and privacy.

clue.text: Stay true

definitions.meaning: to stay a flow of blood is to stop it

explanation.surface: An instruction to remain faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Stemming a wound's bleeding is one meaning; a loyal, steadfast ally is the other.

clue.text: Confirm drink left on board

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone verifies that a drink was left aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To back up or corroborate a claim is to confirm it.

clue.text: Urge free seconds as handouts for journalists

parts.note: to urge is to press
to free is to release

explanation.surface: Someone urges that seconds be given away free to reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Official statements issued to newspapers are handed to reporters for publication.

clue.text: Cleaner must be keener after reprimands

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the reprimands

parts.note: to carpet someone is to reprimand them
to keen is to wail in grief, so a keener is a weeper

explanation.surface: A cleaner must be sharper after being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keener' looks like an adjective, more eager, but is one who keens, or weeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-pushed device with rotating brushes cleans rugs and floors.

clue.text: Extra butter, say, in general

parts.note: in cricket a wide is an extra, a run not scored off the bat
butter is an example of a spread

explanation.surface: More butter is called for generally.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket wide, a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, gives the side a free run, an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent and common everywhere is general rather than limited.

clue.text: At home, authorise first-class returns, getting badges

parts.note: in means at home
to sign is to authorise

indicators.note: returns means read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: At home, someone signs off on excellent returns and is given medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Emblems of rank or office are worn as badges.

clue.text: Runs in a false retreat

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a sham is something false
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone flees during a fake withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu hermitage is a religious retreat for spiritual practice.

clue.text: Fleece cleaner?

parts.note: a fleece is a sheep's coat, and the bath it is plunged into cleans it of parasites

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' suggests a jacket, or swindling, but means a woolly coat on a farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers plunge flocks into a chemical bath to rid their wool of pests.

clue.text: Thrill old lover with quote

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: A former partner delights someone by quoting a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or arouse someone is to give them a thrill.

clue.text: Co-worker clamps over line that's added to engine

indicators.note: to clamp something is to grip it on both sides

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a worker ant is the commonest crossword worker
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A colleague fixes an overhead line to an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'Co-worker' reads as colleague but splits into two pieces that 'clamps' closes around the over and line.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluid poured into a motor's radiator keeps it from overheating.

clue.text: Heart broken by 'X', bully

indicators.note: a broken word has its letters smashed and reassembled

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A heartbroken ex is a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate or menace someone is to bully them.

clue.text: Determine concentration needs time and, after it, speed

indicators.note: after means the speed follows the it

parts.note: speed is rate

explanation.surface: Measuring concentration needs time, and then speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists measure a solution's strength by adding a reagent until a reaction completes.

clue.text: In grammar he, for example, needs to make firm declaration

parts.note: he is an example of a part of speech standing for a noun
to cement is to make firm

explanation.surface: A man must make a firm statement in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal statement or announcement is a declaration.

clue.text: Jog naked around back of building

indicators.note: around means the naked word wraps round the letter

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone runs naked around the back of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' looks like a run but means a gentle prod.
explanation.definitionFit: A small poke with the elbow is a jog, as in jogging someone's memory.

clue.text: Forward should avoid hot garments

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: forward means brash, pushy

explanation.surface: A forward player should avoid wearing hot clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' suggests a player but means pushy.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporting undergarments for women are items of clothing.

clue.text: Electronic circuits and leads regularly being passed

parts.note: circuits of a track are laps

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter

explanation.surface: Electronic circuits and leads are passed around routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has gone by has passed.

clue.text: Abandon hope as a spider runs out

indicators.note: a spider running out scatters, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An arachnophobe gives up as a spider scuttles away.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up all expectation of success is to be hopeless.

clue.text: Achieved a target, retaining information

indicators.note: the words retain, or keep inside them, the letters needed

explanation.surface: Someone met a goal while keeping the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for analysis are information.

clue.text: Lock up suppliers of drugs and boring writers

parts.note: to pen is to lock up or confine
pushers are drug dealers

explanation.surface: Imprison drug dealers and dull authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerks doing tedious desk work with paper are dull scribes.
